sources.author: Clinical Trials Transformation Initiative (CTTI)
sources.title: AACT pipe-delimited flat-file export of ClinicalTrials.gov, data dated 2026-11-17 (file 20261118_export_ctgov.zip)
supports: Input snapshot for every trial record in this dataset. The downloaded zip has SHA-256 6f80d7298d5e3398852b82b60a31e15a03e138cbd2e564e161740318aa7e3822; downloads require a free AACT account.

Study status, design, posted-results dates, conditions, interventions, facility locations, baseline result groups and baseline measurements were read from the studies, conditions, interventions, brief_summaries, facilities, countries, result_groups, baseline_counts and baseline_measurements tables.

sources.author: Clinical Trials Transformation Initiative (CTTI)
sources.title: AACT: The entire ClinicalTrials.gov registry, in one analyzable database
supports: AACT is a public relational database of ClinicalTrials.gov protocol and results data, refreshed daily, with downloadable full snapshots for registered users.

sources.author: Tasneem A, Aberle L, Ananth H, Chakraborty S, Chiswell K, McCourt BJ, Pietrobon R
sources.title: The database for aggregate analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov (AACT) and subsequent regrouping by clinical specialty. PLoS ONE 7(3):e33677
supports: Describes how AACT was built from the ClinicalTrials.gov registry for aggregate analysis, and that data structure, nomenclature and changes in data collection over time make registry data harder to analyze and interpret.

Describes grouping studies by condition using both MeSH terms assigned by an NLM algorithm and condition terms supplied by sponsors, the two sources compared when choosing this dataset's type 2 diabetes rule.

sources.author: Turner BE, Steinberg JR, Weeks BT, Rodriguez F, Cullen MR
sources.title: Race/ethnicity reporting and representation in US clinical trials: a cohort study. Lancet Regional Health: Americas 11:100252
supports: Among 20,692 U.S.-based ClinicalTrials.gov trials with reported results (registered 2000 to 2020), only 43% reported any race/ethnicity data.
Context for showing missing race and ethnicity as not reported rather than hiding those studies, and for treating reporting as something that varies between trials.

sources.author: Heidari S, Babor TF, De Castro P, Tort S, Curno M
sources.title: Sex and Gender Equity in Research: rationale for the SAGER guidelines and recommended use. Research Integrity and Peer Review 1:2
supports: International guidelines for systematically reporting sex and gender information in study design, analyses, results and interpretation.
Basis for keeping sex and gender as separate fields and keeping each measure under the label the study used.
